subject: Maintainer stipend & HackWeek badge credits — sponsorship request
messages:
From: Ava Goodwin <ava@goodwork.org>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: small maintainer stipends + hackweek badge credits

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re well — I run community programs at the OpenBuild Foundation. We’re organizing a winter HackWeek (Jan 2027) focused on infrastructure and open models. A few of our long-term maintainers are stretched thin and we’d like to offer modest stipends (USD 250–500) to ~12 maintainers to secure sustained effort during the sprint. Separately, we’d love to offer Redwood credits for hack participants to experiment with inference: 1500 token credits per participant for ~200 attendees (we can gate by email).

OpenBuild has run small sponsorships before; our ask is: 1) approval for a one-time maintainer stipend pool funded by Redwood credits converted to a small honorarium we reimburse; and 2) promotional credits for HackWeek participants plus a few project-level trial extensions for selected maintainers.

High-level benefits for Redwood: logo on event page, 3 social posts, a short lightning session slot, and continued visibility in our maintainer newsletters. I’ve attached a short sponsorship summary and a CSV with the badge tiers.

Would you be the right person to evaluate this? If not, can you loop in whoever owns community grants or partnerships? We’re on a tight timeline to finalize budgets by Dec 10.

Thanks —
Ava Goodwin
Community Programs, OpenBuild Foundation
ava@goodwork.org
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: sponsorship_summary.pdf, hackweek_badges.csv

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ava Goodwin <ava@goodwork.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: small maintainer stipends + hackweek badge credits

Thanks Ava — love the focus and the timeline makes sense. Looping in Marissa (Community Grants) so we can surface the ask to finance.

Quick answers up front:
- Maintainer stipends: we typically approve honoraria for recognized maintainers; need a short vetting list and the legal/finance flow (monthly vs one-time).
- Participant credits: we can do a limited promotional credit pool for events; I’ll propose 200 accounts @ 1500 tokens each as a starter, or a 3-month trial extension for selected projects.

Marissa — can you review the attached sponsorship_summary.pdf and hackweek_badges.csv and advise if this fits our current grants budget? Dev in finance will need to confirm conversion approach if we do honoraria reimbursements.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Community Programs Manager | Redwood Inference

Priyom / Dev — forwarding Ava’s note and attachments. I’ve skimmed the sponsorship summary: modest ask, strong community reach, and good promotional alignment. My recommendations:

- Approve a maintainer honorarium pool up to USD 4,000 (covers 12 folks at up to $350 each). Prefer reimbursements to projects via foundation invoicing rather than token-to-cash conversions.
- Approve promotional token credits for 200 HackWeek attendees: allocate a 300k-token promotional pool (1500 tokens * 200).
- Three selected maintainers can receive a 6-month trial extension on Dedicated trial tiers (technical contact required).

Action items:
1) Dev: confirm whether finance can process a $4,000 reimbursement to OpenBuild on invoice and whether we need a PO or SOW. Also confirm whether we can reserve promo tokens on marketing budget vs R&D credits.
2) Priyom: if finance approves, I’ll prepare a short sponsor letter and the DocuSign for the reimbursement terms.

Notes: include a lightweight MOU that requires maintainers to agree to minimal reporting (one post-event support note). Also request a short list of maintainers and their GitHub handles for vetting.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments forwarded: sponsorship_summary.pdf, hackweek_badges.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: small maintainer stipends + hackweek badge credits

Marissa / Priyom — finance OK on the $4,000 reimbursement as long as we receive an invoice from OpenBuild and a brief MOU describing the deliverables for maintainers. No PO required for this size; we’ll route payment via Accounts Payable as standard vendor reimbursement.

Promo tokens: marketing budget can cover the 300k-token pool as a one-off promotional credit. I’ll reserve the credits on our internal grant ledger and generate a credit code for Ava to distribute by Dec 15.

Next steps:
- Priyom: confirm the maintainer list (GitHub handles + email) and whether the three project trial extensions are technical or account-level.
- Marissa: please prepare the sponsor letter and MOU; I’ll sign off and provide the accounting references.

I’ve attached a short term sheet template and the accounting reference ID for the reserved promo credits (REF-RED-2026-12-OBF).

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Manager, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com

Attachments: maintainer-stipend-terms.docx

Ava — great news: finance and partnerships have approved the proposal. Summary of approved items:

- Maintainer honorarium pool: $4,000 (OpenBuild to submit invoice + MOU).
- Promotional credits: 300,000 tokens (approx. 1500 tokens x 200 attendees). We will provide a single redeemable credit code and distribution guidance.
- Trial extensions: up to 3 maintainers selected by OpenBuild can receive a 6-month trial extension; please include technical contact emails so we can provision.

Please send the following to pri...@redwood.com by Dec 12 so we can process before your budget deadline:
1) Short list of maintainers (name, GitHub handle, email).
2) One-page MOU template or bullet deliverables.
3) Invoice for $4,000 (OpenBuild Foundation remit info).

Marissa will issue the sponsor letter and DocuSign once we have the MOU. Dev will send the promo credit code and accounting reference when the invoice is processed.

Thanks for running this — excited to support OpenBuild.

Best,
Priyom Das
